subject: Pilot sizing and deployment split for HealthLane (Dedicated vs Private)
messages:

Cc: procurement@healthlane.com

Subject: HealthLane pilot - isolation requirements and initial asks

Hi Dylan + Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked Redwood's routing/fallback idea but two items are blocking our procurement review:

1) Clear sizing/price comparison between a Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in Redwood-hosted infra) vs a fully Private air-gapped deployment (on-prem or VPC with customer-managed hardware).
2) Ops/process differences and timelines: procurement needs to know what we sign up for (lead times, support model, evidence for SOC2/segregation).

High-level constraints:
- P95 infer latency budget for triage flows: 200ms (max).
- Peak concurrent requests for pilot: ~90 qps (bursty, short-lived).
- PHI flows must be segregated and not leave our network (we can route only PHI to Private).
- Target pilot start: mid-August, procurement needs draft costs by EOD 7/10.

I attached our compliance questionnaire and the pilot traffic sample. Can you send a short matrix that compares: cost, time-to-prod, operational burden, and fallback/DR behavior?

Claire

Head of Engineering Operations | HealthLane Therapeutics

Claire — thanks for the clear constraints. Summary below; attached is a pricing workbook (HL_Infrastructure_Pricing_v3.xlsx) and a short latency sample (prefix_latency_samples.csv). High-level recommendation: run a hybrid pilot (Dedicated for public, Private for PHI) but size the Dedicated pool to be the primary capacity to simplify rollouts and reduce procurement lead time.

Option A — Reserved Dedicated (Redwood-hosted, isolated tenant pools):
- Suggested starting capacity (pilot): 8x A100-80GB equiv (2x nodes with 4 GPUs each) configured for continuous batching and KV cache.
- Expected steady throughput: ~90 qps with average generation length 120 tokens, with batching and cache hit rates ~40%.
- P95 latency estimate: 110–160ms (depends on burst smoothing).
- Time-to-prod: 1–2 weeks (account provisioning + model variant pinning).
- Pros: fastest time, managed infra, easier SLAs and observability.
- Cons: cross-tenant networking (if PHI must stay on-customer network, this requires routing/segmentation rules).
- Estimated monthly cost (pilot config): "$62,500" (in-workbook, includes reserved capacity premium and support add-on).

Option B — Private (Customer-managed or VPC-private control plane):
- Suggested starting capacity (pilot): 12x A100-80GB equiv (3x nodes) to match throughput while accounting for loss of multi-tenant scheduling efficiencies and higher headroom for redundancy.
- Expected steady throughput: ~90 qps with similar perf-tuning; cache effectiveness slightly lower until warmed.
- P95 latency estimate: 100–180ms (networking and on-prem infra variance).
- Time-to-prod: 6–10 weeks (procurement + hardware + networking + validation + SOC2 evidence handoff).
- Pros: full data residency, air-gap option available, meets strict PHI policies.
- Cons: higher upfront OPEX/CAPEX, infra ops burden, longer lead time, patching challenges.
- Estimated first-month all-in cost (pilot config, including integration): "$198,000" (hardware/installation amortized + onboarding professional services).

Ops/Design notes:
- We can reduce GPU counts by up to ~30% with aggressive quantization (int8/4bit) and model distillation — trade-off is potential quality regression; we should include a brief eval run.
- KV cache strategy: prioritize common prefixes (triage prompts). Cache sizing in workbook; recommend warm-up window of 24–36 hrs for pilot to reach target hit rate.
- Fallback: configure smart routing so non-PHI goes to Dedicated and PHI routes to Private; in Dedicated saturation events, we recommend a degraded mode where new PHI requests queue rather than spill to public models.

Next steps:
- Marissa: can you produce a single-page procurement appendix that lists contract terms (commit length, upgrade path, SLA credits)?
- Karthik: please add a short technical annex (KV cache numbers + expected network egress).
- Claire / Procurement: if you can confirm the SOC2 evidence checklist items you need, Monica will be our point for evidence delivery.

Im happy to jump on a short call to walk through the workbook tomorrow.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Lead Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Dylan / Marissa — small technical addendum for the procurement appendix: 

1) Cache sizing: for the pilot traffic sample Claire shared, a 12GB KV cache (per node) should give ~38–45% prefix hit for triage prompts. Workbook assumes 12GB cache on Dedicated nodes and 8GB on Private nodes given memory constraints.
2) Utilization target: recommend provisioning at 60–75% of peak token throughput to preserve headroom for spikes; that drives the 8 vs 12 GPU split above.
3) Network/DR: Private deployments frequently require an out-of-band support VPN for triage during incidents; this adds ~2–3 business days for approvals in most large healthcare orgs.
4) Rollout risk: canary to 10% of traffic for 72 hours; if model quality/regressions occur, have an automatic fallback to a smaller model family (fewer tokens, lower cost).

Ill attach a one-page tech annex to the drive link and flag the exact cache numbers in the pricing workbook.

Karthik
Sr. Deal Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: tech_annex_kv_cache.pdf (pdf)

Dylan — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few procurement-level clarifications:

- We cannot accept any model outputs derived from PHI to transit Redwood public infrastructure. Any routing that risks egress needs to be disabled.
- We need a firm commitment on lead time and an option for an SLA credit in the pilot contract if Availability < 99.5% for PHI routes. Whats Redwoods standard SLA credit and how would that apply to a Dedicated pool?
- Is there a short-term approach to get pilot started faster if the Private path slips (e.g., onboard PHI-only to a customer VPC with an accelerated validation checklist)?

Procurement requested the pricing workbook and a clear breakdown of one-time vs recurring costs. If you can get a revised appendix by 7/10 EOD that separates these and lists the minimum commit term for the pilot price, that would help.

Tom Reyes
Sr. Procurement Manager | HealthLane Therapeutics

Tom / Claire — thanks, noted. Quick summary of measurable deliverables and owners so procurement has a single list: 

1) Procurement appendix (Marissa) — separates one-time vs recurring, shows monthly headcount/ops assumptions, and lists the minimum commit term for pilot pricing (suggested 3 months). Target: 2028-07-10 EOD.
2) SOC2 + evidence delivery (Monica) — will provide the SOC2 Type II package and a short evidence map showing which artifacts satisfy HealthLanes checklist items. Monica will also confirm what Redwood can deliver for on-prem validation.
3) Technical annex (Karthik) — KV cache numbers, utilization target, and canary rollout steps.
4) Contract-level SLA: Redwood standard pilot SLA credit for Availability < 99.5% is a pro-rated credit up to 10% of monthly fees for the affected service. For Dedicated pools we can narrow the target and define a separate credit ladder; legal is OK to draft an exception for pilot deals but will need procurement sign-off.

Fallback / acceleration: we can stand up a customer-specific VPC (Redwood Private, customer-managed networking) in ~3 weeks if procurement approves accelerated security onboarding and we accept a limited initial feature set (no automated marketplace integrations). That path reduces the time-to-prod vs full on-prem and preserves PHI residency.

Marissa / Monica / Karthik — please coordinate offline and publish the revised appendix and evidence link to the Drive doc by EOD 7/10. Claire / Tom — if helpful, I can host a 30-minute call Wednesday to walk procurement through the appendix.

Thanks,
Dylan
Lead Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
